title: Choice Strength in Baire, Urysohn, Stone, and Tychonoff

items.title: Dependent multiple choice in finite-level tree form

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: DMC in tree form says every pruned height-omega tree with nonempty levels has a subtree with nonempty finite levels, without requiring the subtree itself to be pruned. In successor-menu form it says every serial relation on a nonempty set has nonempty finite menus satisfying the forward-successor condition. Subtree levels are predecessor-coherent, but leaves must be removed before they are successor menus.
items.proof_plan: Define the R-chain tree, levels, pruning, successor menus, and predecessor coherence. Distinguish downward coherence, which every subtree inherits, from the forward-successor property, which requires pruning to nodes that continue.
items.axiom_base: ZF; DMC is the principle defined

items.title: The tree and successor-menu formulations of DMC are equivalent

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: Over ZF, the finite-level subtree and coherent finite successor-menu forms of DMC are equivalent.
items.proof_plan: Take levels in one direction. Conversely tag menu elements by stage and close each finite menu under its finitely many predecessors; finite unions and images of finite sets are finite in ZF, and coherence gives pruning.

items.title: A nonempty countable set has a padded enumeration in ZF

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: In ZF, every nonempty at-most-countable set D is the range of a sequence s:N→D. The empty set is treated separately and is not asserted to be the range of an N-indexed sequence.
items.proof_plan: Apply the published choice-free equivalence between a nonempty at-most-countable set and a surjective image of N. Its forward proof is explicit: if D is equipotent with N, use the witnessing bijection; if D is finite nonempty, let e:m→D be the witnessing bijection, put d*=e(0), and define s(n)=e(n) for n<m and s(n)=d* for n≥m. This is one finite case distinction on one supplied witness and uses no family choice. If D is empty, do not manufacture a sequence into D; the downstream Baire proof handles the empty ambient space before invoking this lemma.

items.title: Separable complete metric spaces are Baire in ZF

references.title: Marianne Morillon, Synthese
references.locator: Section 2.1, p.5, choice-strength context; separable proof supplied locally

items.statement: In ZF, every separable complete metric space is Baire.
items.proof_plan: If X is empty the Baire conclusion is immediate. Otherwise separability supplies one at-most-countable dense D, which is nonempty because X is; the preceding lemma converts that single witness, with its finite padding case explicit, into a fixed dense sequence. Recursively take the lexicographically least center-index/rational-radius pair whose closed ball lies in the previous open set intersected with the next dense open set and whose radius is at most 2^(-n-2). Existence follows from density and metric regularity; least-number choice is definable. The centers are Cauchy and completeness puts their limit in all nested closed balls. Use the explicit center sequence for Cauchyness and completeness; no arbitrary Cantor-chain intersection theorem or countable choice.
items.axiom_base: ZF; the one supplied dense set, explicit padding, and least-number selection replace DC

items.title: Metacompactness: every open cover has a point-finite open refinement

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice
references.locator: Definitions of refinement and effective metacompactness, printed pp. 8-9

items.title: DMC makes every compact Hausdorff space Baire

references.title: David H. Fremlin, Dependent multiple choice and Baire's theorem (following Fossy and Morillon)
Fossy and Morillon, The Baire category property and some notions of compactness

items.statement: ZF+DMC proves every compact Hausdorff space Baire.
items.proof_plan: Use Fremlin Proposition 2 verbatim. The Hausdorff hypothesis and the preceding compact-Hausdorff theorem first make X regular (indeed normal); this is the exact separation input. For dense open G_n and nonempty open G put G'_k=intersection_{j<k}G_j and let V be the nonempty open subsets of G. Declare U succeeds V when some k has closure(V) contained in U intersect G'_k while U is not contained in G'_k. Unless an open subset already lies in every G_k, regularity makes this relation serial. DMC supplies finite menus V_n; prune them to coherent nonempty finite menus V'_n. Induction on n shows every member of V'_n lies in G'_n. The finite unions W_n of their closures are nonempty closed and decreasing, so countable compactness, hence compactness, gives a point of G intersect intersection_n G_n. All selections are finite or supplied by DMC.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DMC; DMC supplies coherent finite refinement menus

items.title: Compact Hausdorff Baire implies DMC

references.title: David H. Fremlin, Dependent multiple choice and Baire's theorem (following Fossy and Morillon)
Fossy and Morillon, The Baire category property and some notions of compactness

items.statement: Over ZF, if every compact Hausdorff space is Baire, then DMC holds.
items.proof_plan: Reproduce Fremlin Theorem 4, including its separation bookkeeping. Give the tree T the discrete topology, so it is locally compact Hausdorff; the one-point-compactification theorem makes A=T union {infinity} compact Hausdorff. The product topology and Hausdorff-product lemma make X=A^omega Hausdorff, and the hereditary lemma makes its closed subspace K Hausdorff. Here K is the closed set whose non-infinity coordinates form an increasing T-chain. If K is compact, it is therefore within the assumed compact-Hausdorff Baire class, and the open dense sets G_n={x in K: some non-infinity coordinate occurs at or after n} have a common point, giving a branch. If K is not compact, start with a downward-directed family E of nonempty closed subsets of X with empty intersection, enlarged by all forbidden-comparability complements. Recursively adjoin the infinity fibre at coordinate n whenever every projection contains infinity. For the resulting E*, let D be the coordinates whose infinity fibre is absent and F_n=intersection{pi_n[E]:E in E*}; each F_n is finite nonempty. Prove D infinite, since otherwise fixing the finitely many F_n and infinity elsewhere gives a cluster point of E*. Directedness and the forbidden-comparability complements show that for m<n in D every s in F_m has an extension in F_n. Enumerate D and prune successive F_n to coherent nonempty finite levels; their downward closure is a height-omega subtree with finite levels. Lemma 3 converts this tree form to DMC. This is a complete ZF dichotomy and does not assume the product X compact. At stage n, a finite Boolean expression tests only finitely many node labels at coordinate n and has no infinity test there; replacing an untested value by infinity proves any projection omitting infinity is finite. Use unique predecessors, not unique successors. Finite witness selection is explicitly ZF finite choice; product nonemptiness uses the constant infinity point.

items.title: Compact Hausdorff Baire is equivalent to DMC

references.title: Fossy and Morillon, The Baire category property and some notions of compactness
David H. Fremlin, Dependent multiple choice and Baire's theorem (following Fossy and Morillon)

items.statement: Over ZF, every compact Hausdorff space is Baire iff DMC.
items.proof_plan: Combine the preceding two proof-bearing directions. The forward proof spends exactly DMC; the reverse uses the compact/noncompact dichotomy for K and no choice principle. No Recorded catalogue item is used.

items.title: DC is equivalent to Baireness of compact-Hausdorff products

references.title: Horst Herrlich and Kyriakos Keremedis, Products, the Baire category theorem, and the axiom of dependent choice
references.locator: Definitions and Theorem 4, journal pp. 771-775 (scan pp. 1333-1337)

items.statement: Over ZF, DC is equivalent to every product, including the empty product, of compact Hausdorff spaces being Baire.
items.proof_plan: Forward: reproduce Herrlich-Keremedis Theorem 4. The empty product is Baire. In a nonempty product fix x. For a basic open B and dense opens D_n, use the regular pseudo-bases of compact Hausdorff factors to define the serial relation on quadruples (n,F,(B_i),(mathcal B_i)): the next finite-support cylinder has closures nested coordinatewise and lies in B intersect D_n. DC gives a chain. Its support F=union_n F_n is countable under DC; for each i in F the nested closures form a countably based regular filter meeting every pseudo-base, hence have nonempty intersection. Countable Choice, implied by DC, chooses b_i from these intersections, while x supplies off-support coordinates. The resulting product point lies in B intersect intersection_n D_n. Reverse: for a serial relation on A, each alpha A=A union {infinity} is compact Hausdorff and the assumed countable product X=(alpha A)^omega is Baire. A^omega is the intersection of the open dense coordinate sets {x:x(n) in A}; every open dense subset of A^omega is the trace of an open dense subset of X, so A^omega is Baire. Apply the published Blair sequence-space converse to extract an R-chain. This proves DC and avoids citing Theorem 3 as a black box. The theorem makes no nonemptiness claim for a product of nonempty factors.

items.title: DMC implies Urysohn's lemma

references.title: David Fremlin, Dependent multiple choice and Baire's theorem
references.locator: Definition 1 and Proposition 2 p.1: menu formulation and pruning

references.title: alg-d, Urysohn no hodai
references.locator: Theorem 5 p.3: intersection strategy; level-alignment proof supplied locally

items.statement: ZF+DMC proves Urysohn's lemma for normal spaces.
items.proof_plan: DMC menus may start at mixed levels. Keep the least represented initial level, recursively retain successors, then recover earlier levels by even-coordinate projections. The resulting finite menus have exact dyadic levels and both coherence directions. Intersect coordinates, set U0 empty and U1 X, and apply the dyadic scale lemma; handle both endpoints explicitly.

items.title: DMC versus DC over ZF remains open

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: DC implies DMC over ZF. Strictness is known in ZFA, but whether DMC implies DC in ZF is open; no ZF strictness is asserted.
items.proof_plan: Use the existing DC-to-finite-selections theorem and record Morillon's open question exactly.

items.title: Brunner's ordered Läuchli permutation models

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen
Philipp Kleppmann, Free Groups and the Axiom of Choice

items.statement: Define Brunner's ordered permutation models P(A,G,I), requiring the support ideal I to contain singleton supports, be downward and finite-union closed, and be G-invariant so its stabilizer filter is normal. Two instances are distinguished: real-ordered atoms with the G-invariant ideal generated by countable compact supports for Countable Choice, and rational-ordered atoms with the G-invariant finite-support ideal for the BPI separation.
items.proof_plan: Specify the ground-model real and rational order types, countable-compact-generated and finite support ideals, and verify normality. Define the internal closed atom interval [a,b]_A with atom endpoints, verify hereditary symmetry, and use Brunner §1.1 for strongly connected. No ambient Dedekind completion or choice/separation theorem is assumed in this definition; subsequent items owe those properties. Interpret the construction internally in any ZFA+AC model; verify the ZFA axioms by the local relativized formula argument, using the published transitive FM theorem only in its stated transitive case.
items.axiom_base: ZFA+AC metatheory; target permutation models of ZFA

items.title: Brunner's models satisfy the required choice and Urysohn obstructions

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: The real-ordered countable-compact-support model satisfies Countable Choice, and both it and the rational finite-support model contain a nondegenerate compact linearly ordered normal space on which every real-valued continuous function is constant; hence Urysohn's lemma fails.
items.proof_plan: Ground componentwise compression gives a countable compact common support and a hereditarily symmetric choice graph. Prove real interval compactness by ground compactness; prove internal rational order completeness from finite supports and derive compactness by the supremum finite-cover argument. Continuous maps are constant on support-complement orbits; finite continuity joins handle the rational case, countable image and ground IVT handle the real case. Endpoint atoms obstruct Urysohn. Interpret every argument internally in M, using the owning definition's membership-closed hereditarily symmetric interpretation and pure kernel, without an external transitive-ground assumption.
items.axiom_base: Ground ZFA+AC; conclusions interpreted in the respective symmetric ZFA models.

items.title: Extreme amenability yields BPI in finite-support permutation models

references.title: Andreas Blass, Partitions and Permutation Groups
Martin Kleppmann, The Development of the Concept of Amenability
references.locator: Chapter 3, fixed-point formulation of extreme amenability

items.statement: Work internally in an arbitrary model M of ZFA+AC, with no external transitivity assumption. If every pointwise stabilizer of a finite atom set is internally extremely amenable in the pointwise-convergence topology, then the associated hereditarily symmetric finite-support interpretation satisfies BPI.
items.proof_plan: Work internally in an arbitrary model of ZFA+AC. For each nontrivial supported Boolean algebra, internal AC supplies the compact prime-ideal space as a closed subspace of the cube 2^B. Prove joint action continuity using a coset fixing the finite supports of the inverse images of the finitely many cylinder coordinates. Extreme amenability of the relevant finite stabilizer gives a fixed prime ideal; invariance supplies finite support, and elementwise supports make the ideal hereditarily symmetric. Every construction and fixed-point assertion is internal, so no external transitivity of the ground is required.
items.axiom_base: ZFA+AC metatheory; target permutation model satisfies ZFA+BPI

items.title: Finite stabilizers in Aut(Q,<) are extremely amenable

references.title: Kechris, Pestov, and Todorcevic, Fraïssé limits, Ramsey theory, and topological dynamics of automorphism groups
Andreas Blass, Partitions and Permutation Groups

items.statement: Aut(Q,<), and every pointwise stabilizer of a finite subset of Q, is extremely amenable in the pointwise-convergence topology.
items.proof_plan: Apply the KPT correspondence. The age of (Q,<) is the class of finite linear orders; its objects are rigid. Its Ramsey property is exactly finite Ramsey: color embeddings of the a-point order into an N-point order, identify them with a-subsets, and take a homogeneous b-subset. Hence Aut(Q,<) is extremely amenable. A finite point stabilizer is the finite direct product of automorphism groups of the open rational intervals cut out by the support, each order-isomorphic to Q; prove directly that a finite product of extremely amenable groups has a fixed point by taking fixed points one factor at a time. Therefore every required open stabilizer is extremely amenable.

items.title: The Läuchli Urysohn obstruction is injectively boundable

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: The existence of Brunner's specified normal non-Urysohn space admits an atom-blind typed transfer certificate and a fixed absolute relative-rank bound below omega+omega.
items.proof_plan: Expand ordered pairs, order cuts, the topology, closedness, normality, continuity, and real-valued function graphs into membership formulas. Carry the ordered cut space, topology, its two endpoint closed sets, and all candidate real-valued function graphs as named sorts below V_{omega+omega}(A union omega). Verify that atom images are treated opaquely, the pure real interval is fixed, and every quantified object lies in a carried sort. The same typed formula says in the target that the carried space is normal and has no separating continuous real map. This supplies the exact certificate missing from the generic transfer theorem.

items.title: Pincus transfer for BPI and injectively boundable conjunctions

references.title: David Pincus, Zermelo–Fraenkel consistency results by Fraenkel–Mostowski methods
David Pincus, Adding dependent choice
references.locator: Theorem 4 and note added in proof, p. 145

references.title: Eleftherios Tachtsis, The Boolean prime ideal theorem does not imply the extension of almost disjoint families to MAD families
references.locator: Definitions 5.2–5.3, Fact 5.4, and Theorem 5.5, printed pp. 110–111

items.statement: For a permutation model of ZFA, a finite conjunction of certified injectively boundable sentences transfers to a model of ZF. BPI may be conjoined as a named exceptional clause, and Tachtsis's stronger theorem permits the simultaneous conjunction BPI and Countable Choice. No Countable-Choice-only exception, arbitrary ZFA truth, full Choice, or uncertified sentence is transferred.
items.proof_plan: Use Pincus's fact that each certified boundable statement is injectively boundable, retain the finite list of certificates, and apply the cited transfer theorem to that conjunction alone, with BPI, or with the simultaneous BPI-and-AC_omega exception. Tachtsis Theorem 5.5 licenses only the simultaneous BPI-and-AC_omega form, so never transfer AC_omega by itself.
items.axiom_base: Formal relative consistency from ZFA permutation models to ZF

items.title: Relative consistency of Countable Choice without Urysohn's lemma

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+Countable Choice+failure of Urysohn's lemma is consistent.
items.proof_plan: Use the verified constructible-universe reduction to obtain a ZFC+GCH ground model from Con(ZF), expand it by the ordered atom set, and form Brunner's real-ordered countable-compact-support permutation model. The preceding support calculation proves Countable Choice and supplies a compact linearly ordered normal Läuchli continuum with no Urysohn separator. Encode the latter by the preceding atom-blind fixed-rank certificate, and apply the explicit AC_omega clause of the Pincus transfer theorem to that conjunction; this is exactly the external transfer Brunner invokes in the concluding paragraph of §3.4(a). No formal proof-reduction theorem is invoked without a verified code map. FA: use countable completeness and an internal tagged ZFA hierarchy with atoms ordered as the ground real line; no transitive-model or internally countable real-order assumption.

items.title: Relative consistency of BPI without Urysohn's lemma

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen
Andreas Blass, Partitions and Permutation Groups

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+BPI+failure of Urysohn's lemma is consistent.
items.proof_plan: From Con(ZF), use the constructible-universe reduction and first-order completeness to obtain a possibly externally ill-founded model M of ZFC+GCH. Inside M build the tagged ZFA+AC universe over rationally ordered atoms, then form the finite-support Läuchli model. The arbitrary-ground extreme-amenability theorem proves BPI internally, while Brunner's certified obstruction refutes Urysohn's lemma. Pincus transfer sends the conjunction to an atom-free ZF model. The tagged interpretation is the transitive-ground bridge; no external well-foundedness or unprovided proof-code reduction is assumed.

items.title: Brunner's endpoint obstruction also refutes bounded Tietze extension

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: For Brunner's compact normal ordered continuum X with its distinct closed endpoint sets A and B, the continuous map g:A∪B→[0,1] that is 0 on A and 1 on B has no continuous extension to X. Consequently Con(ZF) implies both Con(ZF+Countable Choice+failure of bounded Tietze extension) and Con(ZF+BPI+failure of bounded Tietze extension).
items.proof_plan: In the closed subspace A∪B, each of A and B is clopen because it is the complement of the other closed set, so the displayed two-valued g is continuous. Any continuous extension G:X→[0,1] would equal 0 on A and 1 on B and hence would be the nonconstant separator excluded by Brunner's lemma. For each transferred model, use the normal space and nonseparable closed pair stated by the corresponding Countable Choice or BPI relative-consistency theorem: the same two-valued map on that pair is continuous, while any extension would be a forbidden separator. Do not claim that the transferred witness is literally the original ZFA continuum or assert an unqualified ZF counterexample.

items.title: The Good-Tree-Watson symmetric Stone model

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice

items.statement: Fix a regular uncountable lambda in the ZFC ground model (for DC take lambda=omega_1). Let P=Fn(lambda times R times lambda times lambda,2,lambda), ordered by reverse inclusion, let B=RO(P), and use the Good-Tree-Watson automorphism group with the normal filter generated by pointwise stabilizers of subsets of lambda times R times lambda of size below lambda. Its hereditarily symmetric interpretation contains generic subsets x_{xi,r,alpha} of lambda, the families X_{xi,r}, and metric components R_xi whose metric is transported from the real parameter r.
items.proof_plan: Use the regular-lambda forcing and supports from the paragraph after Good-Tree-Watson Theorem 3. Correct the nonclosed identity/reflection description to independent affine isometries on each xi-component, with arbitrary fibre permutations. Verify group closure/inverses, action on forcing and RO(P), normality and ground-model <lambda-completeness of the support filter. Define H explicitly, distinguish the ground M from component family script R, prove generic subsets distinct by fresh coordinates, and verify hereditary symmetry of all canonical objects and the invariant transported metric. Sequence closure and Stone failure are later obligations.
items.axiom_base: ZFC metatheory; target symmetric model ZF+DC

items.title: The Good-Tree-Watson symmetric model is closed under omega-sequences from the full extension

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice
references.locator: Theorem 3 and the regular-lambda generalization immediately following it, printed p. 6; reduction to Jech Lemma 8.5

references.title: Thomas J. Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.statement: In the regular-lambda Good-Tree-Watson construction, if beta<lambda and g belongs to the full P-generic extension, has domain beta, and every value g(xi) belongs to the symmetric model N, then g belongs to N. In particular, for lambda=omega_1 the conclusion holds for omega-sequences.
items.proof_plan: For each coordinate form the downward set of conditions forcing equality to an HS name. Adjoin conditions with no extension in that set, fuse through these dense sets in M, and use generic directedness to exclude every avoidance alternative. One common q in H then licenses a ground sequence of HS names and small supports via Collection and AC. Their union supports an HS graph name evaluating to g.
items.axiom_base: ZFC metatheory; closure conclusion inside the symmetric extension

items.title: The symmetric Stone model has no componentwise proper selector

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice
references.locator: Claim 1.3, printed pp. 4-5, with the regular-lambda replacement specified after Theorem 3 on printed p. 6

items.statement: No symmetric function chooses a nonempty proper subset of every distinguished metric component.
items.proof_plan: Follow Claim 1.3 with finite/omega replaced uniformly by <lambda/lambda. Take a <lambda-sized support e for a supposed selector and choose xi outside its first-coordinate projection. Strengthen once to decide X_{xi,r} selected and X_{xi,s} unselected. If C is the <lambda-sized set of third coordinates used by that condition in the xi-block, swap C with a disjoint copy C' while reflecting r and s only in that block. This source-authorized coordinate-local automorphism fixes e and the selector name; its image condition reverses the two decisions. The original and image conditions are compatible because their xi-block third-coordinate supports are disjoint and the automorphism is the identity elsewhere, so their union forces a contradiction.

items.title: Relative consistency of DC with failure of Stone's theorem

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice
Thomas J. Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+DC with a metrizable nonparacompact space is consistent; the connected-component witness used here is not zero-dimensional.
items.proof_plan: Invoke Good--Tree--Watson's published relative-consistency theorem in its regular-lambda form with lambda=omega_1; do not infer a transitive ground model from bare consistency. Sequence closure gives DC. On the metric sum use the fixed cover by radius-1/3 balls. A locally finite refinement has finitely many relevant boundaries near each point; recursively shrink an open neighbourhood to avoid them, making the canonical boundary-complement S_xi nonempty. A nonempty refinement member lies in a proper component ball, so connectedness gives a boundary point and makes S_xi proper. The selector obstruction rules out the refinement. FA: the refinement explicitly covers X; start boundary avoidance with W inside its clopen component and prescribe the DC starting point. Transitive presentation is conditional, while the published consistency theorem supplies the external bridge.
items.axiom_base: External relative consistency over Con(ZF); target ZF+DC

items.title: Corson's ordered-rational permutation model

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem
Philipp Kleppmann, Free Groups and the Axiom of Choice

items.statement: The atoms are the ordered rational Urysohn metric space; automorphisms preserve order and metric, and finite supports generate the symmetric model.
items.proof_plan: Record the rational ordered Urysohn metric space U_Q^<, its order-and-metric automorphism group, the finite-support normal filter, and the resulting ZFA permutation universe. The order rigidifies finite metric structures; do not assert that the metric and order topologies coincide. Do not conflate Aut(U_Q^<) with Aut(Q,<); its extreme amenability is supplied separately through the ordered-metric Fraïssé/Ramsey theorem. Verify the ZFA axiom schemes internally, including supported Separation, Power Set and Replacement; the published FM theorem supplies only the transitive-ground special case.
items.axiom_base: Internal ZFA+AC ground with countably infinite atom set; HS satisfies ZFA, with no assertion of AC in HS.

items.title: Corson's rational metric space is not metacompact

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem

items.statement: In Corson's permutation model, the rational Urysohn metric space has an open cover with no point-finite refinement.
items.proof_plan: Follow Corson §2.2 exactly. Use the cover by radius-1/2 balls, assume a point-finite open refining cover, and fix a nonempty finite support E. Choose a beyond E at constant distance D+4, where D=diam(E). For arbitrary n, choose V containing a and m with B(a,1/m) subset V; with K=nm embed the ordered rational chain a_0<...<a_{3K}=a having distances |i-j|/K and constant distance D+4 from E. Extend the shift fixing E to an automorphism phi. The last n chain points lie in V, so a lies in phi^j(V) for j<n. If L is the first chain index in V, the diameter-at-most-1 refinement condition gives 2K<=L<=3K-n+1, and the points a_{L+j} distinguish the n sets phi^j(V). Arbitrary finite injections into the family through a contradict point-finiteness.

items.title: Aut(U_Q^<) is extremely amenable

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem
Jaroslav Nešetřil, Metric spaces are Ramsey
Kechris, Pestov, and Todorcevic, Fraïssé limits, Ramsey theory, and topological dynamics of automorphism groups

items.statement: Assume AC. The pointwise-convergence group Aut(U_Q^<), and every finite point stabilizer required by its finite-support permutation model, is extremely amenable.
items.proof_plan: Use the correctly quantified Ramsey property: for each finite A,B and colour count k there is an extension C with C→(B)^A_k. The age of U_Q^< is the rigid class of finite linearly ordered rational metric spaces, so Nešetřil's theorem and KPT Theorems 4.7/6.16 give extreme amenability of the full group G. For a finite support E, H=fix(E) is open in the pointwise-convergence topology. Prove directly under AC that open subgroups of an extremely amenable group are extremely amenable: for a compact Hausdorff H-flow X, the closed coinduced subspace {Phi in X^G: Phi(hg)=h Phi(g)} is nonempty and compact by choice and Tychonoff; right translation makes it a compact G-flow, and a G-fixed function is constant with H-fixed value at the identity. Feed this exact stabilizer conclusion to the preceding BPI theorem. The topology is pointwise convergence on the discrete underlying set. Use the general topological closed-subspace theorem, and explicitly verify Hausdorffness of the coinduced space.

items.title: Corson's Stone obstruction is ordinal boundable

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem

items.statement: The sentence asserting a Q-valued metric space with an open cover having no point-finite open refining cover is ordinal boundable, with Corson's explicit absolute bound omega+41, and has an atom-blind typed transfer certificate.
items.proof_plan: Reproduce Lemma 5 constructor by constructor: code the underlying atom set, Q-valued metric, rational balls, open cover, candidate refinements, functions and point-finiteness within the stated iterates of the relative hierarchy, ending at V_{omega+41}(A). Relativization captures every possible refinement, not only a chosen one. All atomic tests are equality/membership on carried sorts and the pure rational parameter is fixed, so the formula is atom-blind and meets the typed Jech-Sochor/Pincus certificate.

items.title: Relative consistency of BPI with failure of Stone's theorem

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+BPI with a metrizable nonmetacompact space is consistent.
items.proof_plan: From Con(ZF), obtain by the constructible reduction and first-order completeness a possibly externally ill-founded model M of ZFC+GCH. Inside M build the tagged ZFA+AC universe over its ordered rational Urysohn space and then Corson's finite-support permutation model. The arbitrary-ground extreme-amenability theorem yields BPI; Corson's omega+41 certificate gives an open cover with no point-finite open refinement. Pincus transfer preserves the conjunction in an atom-free ZF model, and the absence of a point-finite open refinement implies absence of a locally finite open refinement and hence failure of Stone's theorem.

items.title: Effective metacompactness for discrete metric spaces implies AC

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice

items.statement: Over ZF, if every open cover of every discrete metrizable space has a point-finite open refining cover equipped with a refinement map, then AC holds.
items.proof_plan: For any family F of nonempty sets use (F times {0}) union (union F times {1}) and cover pairs {(x,1),(S,0)} for x in S in F. The discrete metric has singleton radius-1/2 balls. Through (S,0) there are nonempty finitely many refining-cover members. Their images determine nonempty finitely many elements of S uniquely. This works for overlapping sets. For indexed families compose the resulting function on their set of values; MC implies AC in ZF.

items.title: Products of cofinite spaces are compact exactly under BPI

references.title: Kyriakos Keremedis and Eleftherios Tachtsis, Wallman Compactifications and Tychonoff's Compactness Theorem in ZF

items.statement: Over ZF, BPI is equivalent to compactness of every product of cofinite spaces.
items.proof_plan: Follow Proposition 2.13 using the correct closed basis. If the product is empty it is compact; otherwise fix x in it. Complements of basic product-open sets are finite unions of closed coordinate cylinders, and it suffices to intersect FIP families H of those basic closed sets. BPI extends the generated filter to an ultrafilter F. For each coordinate use the pushforward ultrafilter G_i={B:pi_i^{-1}[B] is in F}, not the projections of arbitrary filter members, and let A_i be the intersection of its closed members. Compactness of the cofinite factor makes A_i nonempty; if A_i is finite, G_i contains a finite set and hence a unique singleton, so A_i is that singleton. Take its unique point, and use the fixed coordinate x_i when A_i is the whole factor. For each H=union_{q in Q} pi_q^{-1}[C_q], finite primeness gives a cylinder in F, so the constructed point lies in H. Conversely use the compact cube 2^{P(S)} for any proper filter on S. Clopen constraints enforce Boolean truth equations and value one on the given filter. Finite satisfiability is evaluation at one point of a finite filter intersection. A point of their compact intersection gives an ultrafilter extension; the existing UFL equivalence yields BPI. No Cantor-cube converse is merely asserted.
items.axiom_base: ZF; BPI is the compared principle

items.title: The isolated-point repair of Kelley's choice space

references.title: Eric Schechter, Handbook of Analysis and Its Foundations, compact T1 product equivalence

items.statement: For every set A, the topological sum X_A=A_c plus {infinity}, where A_c has the cofinite topology and infinity is isolated, is compact T1 and A_c is a closed subspace. This is the corrected Kelley coordinate.
items.proof_plan: The cofinite space A_c is compact in ZF: the empty case is immediate; otherwise take one member of an open cover containing a fixed a in A and cover its finite complement using finite choice. It is T1 because singletons are closed. In the sum, openness means independently that the A-trace is cofinite or empty and the singleton trace is either empty or the singleton. Adding the isolated point preserves compactness by a direct two-piece finite-subcover argument and preserves T1; A_c is clopen because its complement {infinity} is open. Contrast this with an infinite A inside the cofinite topology on A union {infinity}, where A is a proper infinite subset and hence is not closed. Enumerate the single finite complement and the finite list of subcover traces, form the corresponding natural-number-indexed nonempty families, and apply the exact indexed finite-choice lemma separately.

items.title: The compact T1 product theorem is equivalent to AC

references.title: Schechter, Equivalents of the Axiom of Choice

items.statement: Over ZF, AC is equivalent to every product of compact T1 spaces being compact.
items.proof_plan: AC gives product compactness by the published Tychonoff theorem. Conversely, for an arbitrary indexed family (A_i) of nonempty sets form the corrected compact T1 coordinates X_{A_i}. In their product the closed cylinders C_i={x:x_i in A_i} have the finite-intersection property: for a finite J, finite choice selects a_j in A_j and infinity fills every off-J coordinate, defining a point of intersection_{j in J}C_j. Product compactness and the compact-FIP equivalence give a point in intersection_i C_i, whose coordinates form a choice function. Every closedness and FIP supplier is explicit.

items.title: The arbitrary compact product theorem is equivalent to AC

references.title: Schechter, Equivalents of the Axiom of Choice

items.statement: Over ZF, AC is equivalent to every product of arbitrary compact spaces being compact.
items.proof_plan: AC gives arbitrary Tychonoff. Conversely specialize to compact T1 spaces and apply the preceding equivalence. Include the empty product and do not confuse this with compact Hausdorff products, whose strength is BPI.

items.title: False: BPI proves Stone's theorem for metric spaces

items.statement: False: over ZF, BPI implies every metrizable space is paracompact.
items.proof_plan: Invoke the formal relative-consistency theorem. Its ZF model satisfies BPI and contains a metrizable nonmetacompact space, hence an open cover with no point-finite open refining cover. Paracompactness would supply a locally finite, hence point-finite, open refining cover. Thus Stone's conclusion fails in that model and the universal implication is refuted, conditional on Con(ZF).

title: Normal Moore Spaces, PMEA, and Consistency Strength

items.title: Moore spaces and developments

references.title: Dennis K. Burke, The Normal Moore Space Problem

items.statement: A development is a sequence of open covers whose stars at each point form a neighbourhood base. A Moore space is regular T1 and developable. Finite common refinements normalize a development to be decreasing.
items.proof_plan: Define stars and development; at stage n intersect one member from each cover G_0 through G_n, and verify these finite common refinements are open covers with smaller stars and preserve the neighbourhood-base property. Developments directly give first countability.

items.title: Normalized families and collectionwise normality

references.title: Bagaria and da Silva, omega-one-strongly compact cardinals and normality
Fremlin, Real-valued-measurable cardinals

items.statement: A pairwise disjoint family is normalized when every subunion can be separated from its complementary subunion, and separated when it has pairwise disjoint open expansions. Collectionwise normal means every discrete closed family is separated.
items.proof_plan: Fix the closure convention and verify equivalent expansion forms by shrinking. Unions of subfamilies of a discrete closed family are closed, so normality normalizes them; the two-member converse is immediate.

items.title: Metrizable spaces are collectionwise normal

references.title: GMU Math 631 course notes, Axioms of separation
references.locator: Section 14, Theorem 65 and its distance-neighbourhood proof, printed p. 12

items.statement: In ZF, every metrizable space is collectionwise normal.
items.proof_plan: Fix one compatible metric d and a discrete family (F_i) of closed sets; this is one existential witness, not a simultaneous family choice. Put U_i=empty when F_i is empty. For nonempty F_i let H_i=union_{j not equal i}F_j, which is closed because a discrete family is locally finite. If H_i is empty put U_i=X. Otherwise set U_i={x:d(x,F_i)<(1/3)d(x,H_i)}. The two distance functions are 1-Lipschitz, so U_i is open, and discreteness gives each y in F_i a ball avoiding H_i, hence y∈U_i. If x lay in U_i intersect U_j for i not equal j, then F_j⊆H_i and F_i⊆H_j would give d(x,F_i)<d(x,F_j)/3 and d(x,F_j)<d(x,F_i)/3, a contradiction. Thus the U_i are pairwise disjoint open expansions. Empty and singleton families are covered by the explicit cases, and no Choice is used.

items.title: Moore spaces are subparacompact

references.title: Dennis K. Burke, The Normal Moore Space Problem
references.locator: Theorem 2.4 and its proof, printed pp. 2-3

items.statement: In ZFC every Moore space is subparacompact: each open cover has a sigma-discrete closed refinement.
items.proof_plan: Well-order the set U of cover members directly. For a decreasing development G_n define F(U,n) from the W-least cover member containing the point and the condition St(x,G_n) subset U. Development gives coverage; the star test proves every F(U,n) closed and makes each fixed-n family discrete. The countable union over n is the required sigma-discrete closed refinement, and well-ordering the cover is the sole use of AC.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC well-orders the arbitrary cover

items.title: Collectionwise normal Moore spaces are screenable

references.title: R. H. Bing, Metrization of topological spaces

items.statement: In ZFC every collectionwise normal Moore space is screenable: every open cover has a refinement that is a countable union of pairwise disjoint open families.
items.proof_plan: For an open cover H, Bing Theorem 9 well-orders H and, using a decreasing development, constructs closed sets x(h,i): a point belongs when h is the first H-member containing it and every development member at level i through it lies in h. Each X_i={x(h,i):h in H} is discrete, refines H, and the union over i covers X. Collectionwise normality expands each X_i to a pairwise disjoint open family Y_i, chosen so each expansion remains inside the corresponding H-member. Therefore union_i Y_i covers X and refines H, so X is screenable exactly as in Bing Theorem 10. The well-order and simultaneous choices are covered by AC.

items.title: A sigma-cellular base metrizes a normal Moore space

references.title: R. H. Bing, Metrization of topological spaces
references.locator: Theorem 3, printed pp. 178-179, and Theorem 8, printed pp. 181-182

items.statement: Assume ZFC. If a normal Moore space has a base that is a countable union of pairwise disjoint open families, then it is metrizable.
items.proof_plan: For each cellular base level, use the development to exhaust its union by closed sets X_{n,i}. Normal shrinking places each X_{n,i} inside an open D_{n,i} whose closure remains in that union. Intersecting D_{n,i} with the cellular family gives a discrete open family, and all such families form a sigma-discrete basis. Bing's metrization theorem then supplies a compatible metric.

items.title: Normal screenable Moore spaces are metrizable

references.title: R. H. Bing, Metrization of topological spaces
references.locator: Theorems 3, 6, 7, and 8 with proofs, printed pp. 178-182

items.statement: In ZFC every normal screenable Moore space is metrizable.
items.proof_plan: Choose one screening of each development cover. The doubly countable collection of pairwise disjoint open layers is a sigma-cellular base because every screened member refines its development level. Apply the compatible-metric lemma with its actual hypotheses: X is a normal Moore space and has that sigma-cellular base. Normality is essential in the lemma's normal-shrinking step.

items.title: Collectionwise normal Moore spaces are metrizable

references.title: R. H. Bing, Metrization of topological spaces

items.statement: In ZFC, every collectionwise normal Moore space is metrizable.

Apply the preceding full Bing metrization bridge for normal screenable Moore spaces; collectionwise normality includes normality by applying it to a two-element discrete closed family. This composition uses no Recorded-catalogue theorem.

items.statement: A Q-set is an uncountable subset E of the real line every subset of which is relatively G-delta. Bing's tangent-disk construction adjoins E as the boundary of the open upper half-plane and gives boundary points tangent-disk neighbourhoods.
items.proof_plan: Define the Q-set property, including its decreasing-witness normalization V'_n=intersection_{k<=n} V_k starting at V_0, and Bing's point set Z=(R times (0,infinity)) union (E times {0}). For (x,0), use the point together with an open Euclidean disk tangent to the axis at (x,0); ordinary upper-half-plane points retain Euclidean neighbourhoods. Record only this interface here; development, normality, separability and nonmetrizability are proved in a later supplier. The forward existence pointer requires MA plus not CH; verify the tangent disks form a basis.

items.title: MA plus not-CH produces an uncountable Q-set

references.title: Dennis K. Burke, The Normal Moore Space Problem
references.locator: Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.4 with proofs, printed pp. 7-9

items.statement: In ZFC+MA+not-CH, every subset E of the real line of cardinality omega_1 is a Q-set, and hence an uncountable Q-set exists.
items.proof_plan: Fix E={x_alpha:alpha<omega_1} and a countable rational-interval base {W_i}, arranged so every point lies in infinitely many members and every distinct pair lies jointly in only finitely many. Put s(x)={i:x in W_i}. Burke Lemma 4.3, proved by the ccc finite-condition poset and the fewer-than-continuum dense sets supplied by MA, says that for every Y subset E there is d subset omega with s(y) intersect d infinite for y in Y and s(z) intersect d finite for z in E minus Y. Enumerate an infinite d zero-based as p(0)<p(1)<... . Then Y=E intersect intersection_n union_{k>=n} W_{p(k)}; infinite intersection gives every tail membership for y, while finite intersection excludes z. The finite-d case forces Y empty. Thus every Y is relatively G-delta. Since not-CH gives omega_1<continuum, the MA hypothesis applies to all required dense families. Enumerate dyadic pairs without repetition. At a missed midpoint scale the real is a center at every finer scale; otherwise each scale contains it. Diameters shrink and each pair of distinct reals shares only finitely many intervals. Infinite codes with finite pairwise intersection are distinct. Use the continuum cardinal bridge to obtain E.

items.title: Bing's Q-set space is a normal nonmetrizable Moore space

Shrink tangent disks by half to avoid interior accumulation in an opposing closed set, cover remaining off-axis points by countably many rational balls, then disjointify the two countable families. Prove regularity and nonmetrizability directly.

items.statement: Let kappa be infinite, (kappa_n) increasing cofinal in kappa with 2^{kappa_n} < kappa, 2^kappa = kappa^+, E a stationary subset of the cofinality-omega ordinals below kappa^+, and suppose the ladders admit the separation functions m_beta for every beta < kappa^+. Then there is a normal nonmetrizable Moore space.

Define every development level as {B(sigma):sigma in Sigma_n} together with every isolated singleton {q}, so it covers Q and singleton stars refine each isolated point. Verify the uniform-base property, hence regular metacompact Moore structure; reduce normality to the H_Z separations by explicit countable diagonal open sets; prove both club cases with every function evaluation inside its trace domain; and finish nonmetrizability by the Ramsey/Erdos-Rado conflict argument.

items.statement: Under PMEA, a discrete family and downwards-directed neighbourhood families of size below the continuum admit one neighbourhood per point, disjoint across different family members; PMEA-sigma suffices for countable open local bases.

items.title: NMSC gives an inner model with a measurable cardinal

references.title: William G. Fleissner, If all normal Moore spaces are metrizable, then there is an inner model with a measurable cardinal

items.statement: ZFC+NMSC proves there is an inner model with a measurable cardinal.
items.proof_plan: Contrapositively: no inner model with a measurable cardinal implies HYP (supplier item), HYP gives a normal nonmetrizable Moore space, contradicting NMSC.

items.title: Formal consistency lower bound for NMSC

references.title: William G. Fleissner, If all normal Moore spaces are metrizable, then there is an inner model with a measurable cardinal
references.locator: Main theorem and consistency-strength discussion, printed pp. 365-368

items.statement: Con(ZFC+NMSC) implies Con(ZFC plus there is a measurable cardinal).
items.proof_plan: Fix an actual finite target refutation first and let Delta be its finite axiom support. Apply the inner-model theorem only to Delta, choosing one definable nonempty class whose relativizations of those finitely many axioms are provable. Finite interpretation translates that refutation to a source refutation, yielding the external standard-proof-code consistency implication without a uniform class predicate or arithmetic-base compiler.
items.axiom_base: External relative consistency in the metatheory ZFC

items.title: The consistency-strength sandwich for NMSC

references.title: Fremlin, Real-valued-measurable cardinals
Bagaria and da Silva, omega-one-strongly compact cardinals and normality

items.statement: Con(ZFC+NMSC) implies Con(ZFC plus a measurable cardinal), while Con(ZFC plus a strongly compact cardinal) implies Con(ZFC+NMSC).
items.proof_plan: Keep the internal measurable-inner-model consequence, the formal lower consistency implication and the strongly compact forcing upper implication as three separate claims and chain the latter two.

items.title: The omega-one-strongly compact refinement and open gap

references.title: Bagaria and da Silva, omega-one-strongly compact cardinals and normality

items.statement: Bagaria-da Silva prove Con(ZFC plus an omega-one-strongly compact cardinal) implies Con(ZFC+NMSC), via random forcing and PMEA-sigma; whether NMSC reaches that consistency strength is open.
items.proof_plan: Literature context only: Theorem 2.10 gives the pullback, but its Solovay-measure input is sketched and the PMEA-sigma separation modification omitted. It carries no proof load and does not replace the proved strong-compact branch.

title: Normal Moore Spaces, PMEA, and Consistency Strength: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Development stars form a countable local base

references.title: Dennis K. Burke, The Normal Moore Space Problem

items.statement: For metric covers by balls of radius 2^(-n), compute the stars and verify that they form a countable local base.
items.proof_plan: The star contains the radius 2^(-n) ball and is contained in the radius 2^(1-n) ball. Given an epsilon-neighbourhood, choose n with 2^(1-n)<epsilon. Use the exact three metric axioms, Archimedean reciprocal bound and regular T1 metrizable-space supplier; stars are open and handle arbitrary neighbourhoods.

items.title: The three-quarter event calculation in the PMEA proof

references.title: Fremlin, Real-valued-measurable cardinals

items.statement: Two good events of measure above three quarters overlap in positive measure, providing a separating parameter.
items.proof_plan: Compute mu(E intersect F) at least mu(E)+mu(F)-1>1/2, select a point of the overlap, and apply the two opposite closure conditions.

items.title: False: ZFC proves the normal Moore space conjecture

references.title: William G. Fleissner, If all normal Moore spaces are metrizable, then there is an inner model with a measurable cardinal
references.locator: CH instance and complete construction, printed pp. 366-373

items.statement: False relative to Con(ZFC): ZFC proves every normal Moore space metrizable.
items.proof_plan: Use the exact positive-consistency corollary to obtain Con(ZFC+CH) from Con(ZFC). Were ZFC to prove NMSC, weakening would give that theorem in ZFC+CH; concatenate it with the CH theorem producing a normal nonmetrizable Moore space to obtain a ZFC+CH refutation, contradicting consistency.
